1	# VAPO: Value-Model-Based RL Achieves State-of-the-Art on AIME 2024
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05118
     5	
     6	## Overview
     7	
     8	VAPO (Value-model-based Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization) is a reinforcement learning framework developed by ByteDance Seed for training reasoning models with long chain-of-thought (CoT). Built on the Qwen2.5-32B pre-trained model with no SFT data, VAPO achieves a score of 60.4 on AIME 2024 (avg@32), surpassing the previous state-of-the-art DAPO (50) and DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B (47) by more than 10 points. VAPO reaches this performance within only 5,000 training steps and exhibits no training crashes across multiple independent runs.
     9	
    10	## Motivation: Value-Model-Based vs Value-Model-Free
    11	
    12	Value-model-free methods like GRPO and DAPO have been dominant in LLM RL training. They compute advantage based on final trajectory reward and assign it uniformly across all tokens. While effective, this approach has limitations for complex reasoning:
    13	
    14	- **Credit assignment**: Value models enable precise token-level credit assignment, tracing each action's impact on returns. This is critical when subtle step-level errors cause catastrophic failures.
    15	- **Variance reduction**: Value models provide lower-variance estimates per token compared to Monte Carlo methods.
    16	- **Generalization**: A well-trained value model generalizes across samples, improving sample efficiency.
    17	
    18	However, training value models for long-CoT tasks faces three core challenges: (1) **value model bias** from long trajectories and bootstrapped learning, (2) **heterogeneous sequence lengths** requiring different bias-variance tradeoffs, and (3) **reward signal sparsity** where only the final <eos> token receives reward.
    19	
    20	## VAPO Framework Components
    21	
    22	VAPO integrates multiple techniques to address these challenges:
    23	
    24	- **Value-Pretraining**: Pre-trains the value model before RL to reduce initial bias.
    25	- **Decoupled-GAE**: Separates GAE computation to handle value estimation more robustly (from VC-PPO).
    26	- **Length-adaptive GAE** (novel): Dynamically adjusts the λ parameter in GAE based on response length. Short responses use lower λ (lower variance), while long responses use higher λ (lower bias), optimizing the bias-variance tradeoff across heterogeneous lengths.
    27	- **Clip-Higher**: Asymmetric clipping from DAPO that encourages exploration.
    28	- **Token-level Loss**: Normalizes loss at the token level rather than sequence level (from DAPO).
    29	- **Positive Example LM Loss**: Self-imitation learning on correct trajectories.
    30	- **Group-Sampling**: Samples multiple responses per prompt for better baseline estimation (from GRPO).
    31	
    32	## Main Results and Ablation Study
    33	
    34	| Model | AIME24 avg@32 |
    35	|---|---|
    36	| Vanilla PPO | 5 |
    37	| DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B | 47 |
    38	| DAPO | 50 |
    39	| VAPO w/o Value-Pretraining | 11 |
    40	| VAPO w/o Decoupled-GAE | 33 |
    41	| VAPO w/o Length-adaptive GAE | 45 |
    42	| VAPO w/o Clip-Higher | 46 |
    43	| VAPO w/o Token-level Loss | 53 |
    44	| VAPO w/o Positive Example LM Loss | 54 |
    45	| VAPO w/o Group-Sampling | 55 |
    46	| **VAPO** | **60** |
    47	
    48	The ablation reveals that Value-Pretraining is the most critical component (removing it drops from 60 to 11), followed by Decoupled-GAE (drop to 33) and Length-adaptive GAE (drop to 45).
    49	
    50	![VAPO vs DAPO training curves on AIME 2024](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    51	
    52	The training curve shows VAPO consistently outperforms DAPO throughout training and reaches 60% accuracy around step 4,500, while DAPO plateaus near 50% at step 5,500. DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B reaches 47% after approximately 10,000 steps.
    53	
    54	![Mean response length over training](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    55	
    56	VAPO generates longer responses than DAPO (reaching ~6,000 tokens vs ~4,500), suggesting it learns more elaborate reasoning chains.
    57	
    58	## Key Findings
    59	
    60	- **VAPO achieves 60.4 on AIME 2024**, surpassing DAPO (50) and DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B (47) by 10+ points, all on the same Qwen2.5-32B base model with no SFT data.
    61	- **Value-Pretraining is the single most impactful component**, contributing 49 points (from 11 to 60); without it, value-model-based RL barely works.
    62	- **Length-adaptive GAE is a novel and effective technique** that addresses the heterogeneous sequence length problem unique to long-CoT reasoning, contributing 15 points.
    63	- **VAPO is highly training-efficient and stable**, reaching SOTA in ~5,000 steps with zero training crashes across multiple runs, compared to DAPO's ~5,500 steps for a lower score.
    64	- **Value-model-based RL can outperform value-model-free methods** for complex reasoning when the three core challenges (bias, heterogeneous lengths, reward sparsity) are systematically addressed.

    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a 9-slide 16:9 technical presentation on VAPO.
Data-forward, analytical tone for ML researchers and RL practitioners.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette — deep indigo / slate / amber accent (data-forward, technical)
PRIMARY = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x23, 0x7E)      # Deep indigo
SECONDARY = RgbColor(0x5C, 0x6B, 0xC0)    # Medium indigo
ACCENT = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xA0, 0x00)       # Amber accent
DARK = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x1E, 0x1E)         # Near-black
LIGHT = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF6, 0xFA)        # Off-white background
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
GRAY = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xE0, 0xE0, 0xE0)
GREEN = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x7D, 0x32)        # Positive delta
RED = RgbColor(0xC6, 0x28, 0x28)          # Negative delta

MARGIN_LEFT = Inches(0.5)
MARGIN_TOP = Inches(0.4)
MARGIN_RIGHT = Inches(0.5)
MARGIN_BOTTOM = Inches(0.4)

OUTPUT_DIR = "/app/output"
ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "final_deck.pptx")

os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_slide_bg_color(slide, color_rgb):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color_rgb


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(18),
                font_color=DARK, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.italic = italic
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                       font_size=Pt(18), font_color=DARK, font_name="Calibri",
                       bullet_color=ACCENT, line_spacing=1.2):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.level = 0
    return txBox


def add_title_bar(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=""):
    """Add a consistent top title bar with accent underline."""
    # Title bar background
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
        0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(1.15)
    )
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = PRIMARY
    bar.line.fill.background()
    # Send to back
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = bar._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

    # Accent underline
    underline = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
        0, Inches(1.12), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.03)
    )
    underline.fill.solid()
    underline.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
    underline.line.fill.background()
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = underline._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

    # Title text
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(
        MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(0.22),
        SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT - MARGIN_RIGHT, Inches(0.7)
    )
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title_text
    p.font.size = Pt(32)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    p.font.name = "Calibri"

    if subtitle_text:
        p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
        p2.text = subtitle_text
        p2.font.size = Pt(16)
        p2.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
        p2.font.name = "Calibri"
        p2.space_before = Pt(4)

    return Inches(1.25)  # content top offset


def add_footer(slide, page_num, total=9):
    """Add page number and source footer."""
    # Page number
    add_textbox(slide, SLIDE_WIDTH - Inches(1.2), SLIDE_HEIGHT - Inches(0.35),
                Inches(1.0), Inches(0.25),
                f"{page_num}/{total}",
                font_size=Pt(10), font_color=GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    # Source
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, SLIDE_HEIGHT - Inches(0.35),
                Inches(6), Inches(0.25),
                "Source: ByteDance Seed, arXiv:2504.05118",
                font_size=Pt(10), font_color=GRAY)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # Blank
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, LIGHT)

    # Large background shape
    bg = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, SLIDE_HEIGHT
    )
    bg.fill.solid()
    bg.fill.fore_color.rgb = PRIMARY
    bg.line.fill.background()
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = bg._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

    # Accent bar
    ab = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, Inches(3.6), SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.06)
    )
    ab.fill.solid()
    ab.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
    ab.line.fill.background()
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = ab._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(2.2),
                SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT * 2, Inches(1.3),
                "VAPO: Value-Model-Based RL for Advanced Reasoning",
                font_size=Pt(44), font_color=WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Subtitle / result
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(3.75),
                SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT * 2, Inches(0.6),
                "60.4 on AIME 2024  |  Surpasses DAPO by 10+ Points  |  Qwen2.5-32B Base, No SFT",
                font_size=Pt(22), font_color=ACCENT, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Authors / org
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, Inches(5.5),
                SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT * 2, Inches(0.5),
                "ByteDance Seed  ·  arXiv:2504.05118",
                font_size=Pt(18), font_color=RgbColor(0xAA, 0xAA, 0xAA),
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_footer(slide, 1)
    return slide


def build_motivation_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "Why Value Models? Finer Credit Assignment for Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning",
        "Value-model-free methods assign trajectory-level advantage uniformly; value models enable token-level credit assignment"
    )

    # Left column: Value-Model-Free (GRPO / DAPO)
    left_box = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
        MARGIN_LEFT, content_top + Inches(0.2),
        Inches(5.8), Inches(4.8)
    )
    left_box.fill.solid()
    left_box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xF0, 0xF1, 0xF8)
    left_box.line.color.rgb = SECONDARY

    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.2), content_top + Inches(0.35),
                Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
                "Value-Model-Free (GRPO, DAPO)",
                font_size=Pt(20), font_color=PRIMARY, bold=True)

    free_bullets = [
        "• Compute advantage from final trajectory reward",
        "• Assign same advantage to every token uniformly",
        "• High variance for long, heterogeneous CoT lengths",
        "• No fine-grained step-level error attribution"
    ]
    add_bullet_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.2), content_top + Inches(0.85),
                       Inches(5.4), Inches(3.8),
                       free_bullets, font_size=Pt(17), font_color=DARK)

    # Right column: Value-Model-Based (VAPO)
    right_box = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
        MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(6.4), content_top + Inches(0.2),
        Inches(5.8), Inches(4.8)
    )
    right_box.fill.solid()
    right_box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xE8, 0xF5, 0xE9)
    right_box.line.color.rgb = GREEN

    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(6.6), content_top + Inches(0.35),
                Inches(5.4), Inches(0.4),
                "Value-Model-Based (VAPO)",
                font_size=Pt(20), font_color=GREEN, bold=True)

    based_bullets = [
        "• Token-level credit assignment via learned value model",
        "• Lower-variance advantage estimates per token",
        "• Generalizes across samples → better sample efficiency",
        "• Critical when subtle step errors cause catastrophic failure"
    ]
    add_bullet_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(6.6), content_top + Inches(0.85),
                       Inches(5.4), Inches(3.8),
                       based_bullets, font_size=Pt(17), font_color=DARK)

    add_footer(slide, 2)
    return slide


def build_three_challenges_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "Three Core Challenges in Value-Model-Based Long-CoT RL",
        "Long chain-of-thought reasoning exposes fundamental weaknesses in standard value estimation"
    )

    challenges = [
        ("1. Value Model Bias",
         "Long trajectories and bootstrapped learning amplify bias in value estimates, especially early in training.",
         PRIMARY),
        ("2. Heterogeneous Sequence Lengths",
         "Responses vary from hundreds to thousands of tokens; a single bias-variance tradeoff cannot fit all lengths.",
         SECONDARY),
        ("3. Reward Signal Sparsity",
         "Only the final <eos> token receives reward, making credit assignment through long reasoning chains extremely hard.",
         ACCENT),
    ]

    col_width = Inches(3.8)
    gap = Inches(0.35)
    start_x = MARGIN_LEFT

    for i, (title, body, color) in enumerate(challenges):
        x = start_x + i * (col_width + gap)
        # Card background
        card = slide.shapes.add_shape(
            MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
            x, content_top + Inches(0.3),
            col_width, Inches(4.5)
        )
        card.fill.solid()
        card.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xFA, 0xFA, 0xFA)
        card.line.color.rgb = color

        # Colored top bar
        bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(
            MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
            x, content_top + Inches(0.3),
            col_width, Inches(0.12)
        )
        bar.fill.solid()
        bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
        bar.line.fill.background()

        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.15), content_top + Inches(0.55),
                    col_width - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.5),
                    title, font_size=Pt(19), font_color=color, bold=True)

        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.15), content_top + Inches(1.15),
                    col_width - Inches(0.3), Inches(3.0),
                    body, font_size=Pt(16), font_color=DARK)

    add_footer(slide, 3)
    return slide


def build_framework_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "VAPO Framework: Integrated Solutions for Value-Model-Based Reasoning RL",
        "Each component maps directly to one of the three core challenges"
    )

    # Challenge labels (top row)
    challenge_labels = [
        ("Challenge 1: Value Model Bias", PRIMARY),
        ("Challenge 2: Heterogeneous Lengths", SECONDARY),
        ("Challenge 3: Reward Sparsity", ACCENT),
    ]
    col_w = Inches(3.9)
    gap = Inches(0.25)
    start_x = MARGIN_LEFT
    for i, (label, color) in enumerate(challenge_labels):
        x = start_x + i * (col_w + gap)
        add_textbox(slide, x, content_top + Inches(0.15),
                    col_w, Inches(0.35),
                    label, font_size=Pt(15), font_color=color, bold=True,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    # Component boxes mapped to challenges
    components = [
        # (challenge_idx, row, title, description)
        (0, 0, "Value-Pretraining", "Pre-trains value model before RL to reduce initial bias.", PRIMARY),
        (0, 1, "Decoupled-GAE", "Separates GAE computation for more robust value estimation (from VC-PPO).", PRIMARY),
        (1, 0, "Length-Adaptive GAE", "Dynamically adjusts λ based on response length: short → low λ, long → high λ.", SECONDARY),
        (1, 1, "Clip-Higher", "Asymmetric clipping encourages exploration (from DAPO).", SECONDARY),
        (2, 0, "Token-level Loss", "Normalizes loss per token rather than per sequence (from DAPO).", ACCENT),

        (2, 2, "Group-Sampling", "Multiple responses per prompt for better baseline (from GRPO).", ACCENT),

        box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xF8, 0xF8, 0xF8)
        box.line.color.rgb = color

        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.08), y + Inches(0.06),
                    box_w - Inches(0.16), Inches(0.3),

        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.08), y + Inches(0.38),
                    box_w - Inches(0.16), Inches(0.7),

def build_length_adaptive_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "Length-Adaptive GAE: Dynamic λ Adjustment for Variable Response Lengths",
        "Novel technique that optimizes the bias-variance tradeoff across heterogeneous sequence lengths"
    )

    # Left: conceptual explanation
    left_w = Inches(6.0)
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, content_top + Inches(0.3),
                left_w, Inches(0.4),
                "Core Idea", font_size=Pt(22), font_color=PRIMARY, bold=True)

        "• Standard GAE uses a fixed λ for all sequences.",
        "• Long-CoT responses vary wildly in length (hundreds → thousands of tokens).",
        "• Short responses benefit from lower λ → lower variance (reliable but biased).",
        "• Long responses benefit from higher λ → lower bias (more accurate credit).",
        "• Length-Adaptive GAE dynamically sets λ = f(length) per sample."
    ]
    add_bullet_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, content_top + Inches(0.8),

    )

    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
    chart_data.categories = ['Vanilla PPO', 'DeepSeek-R1-Zero\nQwen-32B', 'DAPO', 'VAPO']

    colors = [GRAY, SECONDARY, PRIMARY, GREEN]
    series = chart.series[0]
    for idx, point in enumerate(series.points):
        point.format.fill.solid()
        point.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = colors[idx]

    # Remove legend

    # Key callouts on the right
    callout_x = MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(8.0)
    callout_w = Inches(4.5)

    add_textbox(slide, callout_x, content_top + Inches(0.5),
                callout_w, Inches(0.4),

    result_bullets = [
        "• VAPO: 60.4  —  new SOTA on AIME 2024",
        "• DAPO: 50  —  previous best value-free method",
        "• DeepSeek-R1-Zero: 47  —  same base model",
        "• Vanilla PPO: 5  —  baseline collapse",
        "",
        "• VAPO reaches 60% accuracy by step ~4,500",
        "• DAPO plateaus near 50% at step ~5,500",
        "• Zero training crashes across multiple runs"
    ]
    add_bullet_textbox(slide, callout_x, content_top + Inches(1.0),
                       callout_w, Inches(3.5),
                       result_bullets, font_size=Pt(16), font_color=DARK)

    # Reference to figure
    add_textbox(slide, callout_x, content_top + Inches(4.6),
                callout_w, Inches(0.4),

def build_ablation_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "Ablation: Every Component Matters — Value-Pretraining Alone Adds 49 Points",
        "Component contribution measured by AIME 2024 score drop when removed from full VAPO (60)"
    )

    # Build a waterfall-style table
    rows, cols = 8, 4
    left = MARGIN_LEFT
    top = content_top + Inches(0.4)
    width = SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT - MARGIN_RIGHT
    height = Inches(4.2)

    table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table

    # Column widths
    table.columns[0].width = Inches(4.5)
    table.columns[1].width = Inches(2.2)
    table.columns[2].width = Inches(2.2)
    table.columns[3].width = Inches(3.0)

    headers = ["Configuration", "AIME 2024 Score", "Δ from VAPO", "Relative Impact"]
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell = table.cell(0, i)
        cell.text = h
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.size = Pt(16)
        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = PRIMARY

    data = [
        ("VAPO (full)", "60", "—", "Baseline"),
        ("w/o Value-Pretraining", "11", "-49", "Critical — value model collapses"),
        ("w/o Decoupled-GAE", "33", "-27", "Major — unstable value estimation"),
        ("w/o Length-Adaptive GAE", "45", "-15", "Strong — heterogeneous length mismatch"),
        ("w/o Clip-Higher", "46", "-14", "Moderate — reduced exploration"),
        ("w/o Token-level Loss", "53", "-7", "Minor — sequence-level normalization harm"),
        ("w/o Positive Example LM Loss", "54", "-6", "Minor — less self-imitation signal"),
    ]

    for r_idx, (config, score, delta, impact) in enumerate(data, start=1):
        cells = [config, score, delta, impact]
        for c_idx, val in enumerate(cells):
            cell = table.cell(r_idx, c_idx)
            cell.text = val
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.font.size = Pt(15)
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER if c_idx > 0 else PP_ALIGN.LEFT

            # Row coloring
            if r_idx == 1:  # full VAPO
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xE8, 0xF5, 0xE9)
                p.font.bold = True
                p.font.color.rgb = GREEN
            elif "Value-Pretraining" in val or (c_idx == 3 and "Critical" in val):
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xEB, 0xEE)
                p.font.color.rgb = RED
                p.font.bold = True
            elif r_idx % 2 == 0:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)
            else:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = WHITE

    # Highlight callout below table
    add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, content_top + Inches(4.9),
                width, Inches(0.5),
                "Takeaway: Value-Pretraining is the single most important component. Without it, value-model-based RL barely outperforms Vanilla PPO.",
                font_size=Pt(17), font_color=RED, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    add_footer(slide, 8)
    return slide


def build_takeaways_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg_color(slide, WHITE)
    content_top = add_title_bar(
        slide,
        "Key Takeaways: Value-Model-Based RL Is Back — With the Right Engineering",
        "Implications for the next generation of reasoning model training"
    )

    takeaways = [
        ("1. Value-model-based RL can surpass value-free methods",
         "When bias, heterogeneous lengths, and sparsity are systematically addressed, token-level credit assignment wins."),
        ("2. Length-Adaptive GAE is critical for long-CoT reasoning",
         "A fixed λ cannot serve sequences ranging from hundreds to thousands of tokens; dynamic adjustment adds 15 points."),
        ("3. Value-Pretraining is the single most important component",
         "It contributes 49 points (60 → 11). Without it, the value model collapses and the framework fails."),
        ("4. VAPO is highly training-efficient and stable",
         "Reaches SOTA in ~5,000 steps with zero crashes, versus DAPO’s ~5,500 steps for a lower score."),
        ("5. Implications for future reasoning models",
         "Engineering around value-model challenges unlocks finer credit assignment, enabling longer and more reliable reasoning chains."),
    ]

    y = content_top + Inches(0.3)
    box_w = SLIDE_WIDTH - MARGIN_LEFT - MARGIN_RIGHT
    box_h = Inches(0.95)
    gap = Inches(0.12)

    for i, (title, body) in enumerate(takeaways):
        # Numbered box
        num_box = slide.shapes.add_shape(
            MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
            MARGIN_LEFT, y, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5)
        )
        num_box.fill.solid()
        num_box.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
        num_box.line.fill.background()
        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT, y + Inches(0.05),
                    Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4),
                    str(i + 1), font_size=Pt(20), font_color=WHITE,
                    bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # Text
        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.65), y,
                    box_w - Inches(0.7), Inches(0.35),
                    title, font_size=Pt(18), font_color=PRIMARY, bold=True)
        add_textbox(slide, MARGIN_LEFT + Inches(0.65), y + Inches(0.35),
                    box_w - Inches(0.7), Inches(0.5),
                    body, font_size=Pt(15), font_color=DARK)

        y += box_h + gap

    add_footer(slide, 9)
    return slide


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_motivation_slide(prs)
    build_three_challenges_slide(prs)
    build_framework_slide(prs)
    build_length_adaptive_slide(prs)
    build_main_results_slide(prs)
    build_training_curves_slide(prs)
    build_ablation_slide(prs)
    build_takeaways_slide(prs)

    prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"Saved presentation to {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
